Package index

Special functions

Arbitrary-precision evaluation of the two Meijer-G shapes the whole package reduces to.

g_gamma_chain()
G^{N,0}_{0,N}(z | -- ; b_1,...,b_N) – the gamma-chain shape (s = 1/2).
g_invgamma_chain()
G^{0,N}_{N,0}(z | b_1,...,b_N ; --) – the inverse-gamma-chain shape (s = 1), via the reflection identity = G^{N,0}_{0,N}(1/z | -- ; 1-b).

Reservoir background

The cascade’s temperature law and its dynamics.

f_N()
The reservoir temperature law f_N(T_N), Eq. (33), corrected.
sample_TN()
Ancestral sampling of T_N down the chain, Eq. (30).
sample_conditional()
Draw T_i ~ f(T_i | T_{i-1}), Eqs. (31)/(32).
conditional_pdf()
f(T_i | T_{i-1}), Eq. (31) for s = 1/2 and Eq. (32) for s = 1.
kappa_from_a()
Invert a_i = 2*gamma_i/kappa_i^2 for the noise amplitudes.
simulate_sde()
Euler-Maruyama on the hierarchy dT_i = -gamma_i (T_i - T_{i-1}) dt + kappa_i T_i^s T_{i-1}^{1-s} dW_i, Eq. (29).

Statistical factor

B_N^(s)(E; a) and its tail integral.

B()
B_N^{(s)}(E; a), Eq. (34).
B_tilde()
Btilde_N^{(s)}(E) = beta0 * int_E^inf B_N(E') dE', Eqs. (37)-(38).
B_prime()
dB/dE, Eq. (43): strictly negative, hence s''(B) < 0, Eq. (44).
omega_of()
omega = prod(a_i), Eq. (33). The scalar Eq. (38) leaves alone.
shift()
The parameter shift of Eq. (38): a -> a + 3 - 4s.

Entropy generator

s_tilde()
s~_N^{(s)}(E) = (beta0*E - 1)*B(E) + Btilde(E), Eq. (39).
parametric_curve()
The parametric curve (B(E), s~(E)) – geometric in 1 + beta0*E so both the B ~ 1 knee and the tail are resolved. Outside the three solvable cases E(B) has no closed form, so s(B) exists only as this curve or through E_of_B.
E_of_B()
E such that B(E) = Bval, vectorized over Bval. Well-posed for every (N, a) and both classes because B is strictly decreasing from B(0) = 1 to B(inf) = 0, Eqs. (7)/(43).
make_interpolants()
Build monotone-cubic interpolants of E(B) and s~(B), amortizing the cost of repeated B()/E_of_B() evaluation (each one, worst case, an escalating-precision Meijer-G or quadrature call – see R/meijer.R and R/statfactor.R) over a table built once. Two curves are tabulated, both against log(B), NOT E or B directly:
make_E_of_B()
Convenience wrapper returning just the tabulated E_of_B function.
s_of_B()
s~(E_of_B(Bval)), exact (not tabulated) composition.
s_prime_of_B()
d(s~)/d(B) = beta0*E_of_B(B) - 1, exact via the inverse function (Eq. 43 makes s~ a function of E whose derivative w.r.t. B collapses to this, with no differentiation needed).
S_simplex()
S[p] = sum_i s_of_B(Z*p_i)/Z + c*sum(p_i), Eq. (10). Z (the partition function) is mandatory – it is supplied externally, not recomputed here.
s_boltzmann_shannon()
-B*log(B), Eq. (21): the N=0 / plain-exponential special case, where s~ collapses to this exactly.
s_tsallis_kernel()
s(B) = -(a+1)*(B - B^q), Eq. (63) – the N=1, s=1 exactly-solvable case, q = a/(a+1) the entropy index. Summed over the simplex this is exactly the Tsallis entropy, Eqs. (64)/(67).
q_indices()
The two Tsallis indices for the s=1, N=1 case (Eq. 65) – distinct and must not be conflated: q is the entropy index, q_stat the distribution index.
tsallis_entropy()
The exact Tsallis entropy of a probability vector p, at entropy index q = a/(a+1).

Identifiability and estimation

Recovering the cascade depth from a single marginal.

log_cumulants_theory()
Theoretical kappa_r(log T_N) for r=2..r_max. Independent of T_0 by construction; relies only on the shape vector a and branch s. a may be empty (N = 0), for which all cumulants are 0.
empirical_log_cumulants()
Unbiased sample cumulants k_r of log T for r=2..r_max, via the standard k-statistic (directly comparable to log_cumulants_theory with no finite-sample bias correction).
fit_homogeneous()
Point estimate of (N, a) under the homogeneous model a_i = a, from (kappa2, kappa3). Two equations, two unknowns: kappa3/kappa2 depends on a alone (the N factor cancels), recovered by a 1-D root find; then N = kappa2 / psi'(a) from the scale.
test_depth()
Parametric-bootstrap test of H0: depth = N0 (homogeneous a) against the sample T. Fits a under H0 from kappa2 alone, so the test statistic – observed kappa3 minus the value predicted at (N0, a_hat) – is not tautologically zero. Its null distribution is a parametric bootstrap: simulate n_boot depth-N0 cascades at the fitted shape and refit on each. N sits at the boundary of its domain (a positive integer), so the usual chi-square asymptotics for a likelihood-ratio test do not apply (Self & Liang 1987), hence bootstrap rather than a closed-form p-value.
power_curve()
Simulated power of test_depth at H0: N = N0 against a true cascade a_true (its length is the true depth). Returns a named list n -> power: reject rate under a true deeper cascade, at a shallow null.

Networks

The mixed-Poisson application, depth from a degree sequence alone.

sample_degrees()
Draw a mixed-Poisson degree sequence, D_v | W_v ~ Poisson(lambda*W_v). W is drawn from sample_TN with T0 = 1, so E[W] = 1 and E[D] = lambda exactly.
log_factorial_moment_theory()
log E[W^k], summed over independent levels. Homogeneous case (a_i = a) reduces to N*[log Gamma(a+k) - log Gamma(a) - k*log(a)] for s=1/2, linear in N.
empirical_log_factorial_moments()
(lambda_hat, c(L_2,...,L_k_max)) with L_k = log(Ehat[W^k]). lambda_hat is the sample mean of D (exact since E[W]=1). The falling-factorial product is exactly 0 whenever D < k, so no special-casing of small degrees is needed.
fit_homogeneous_network()
Recover (N, a, lambda) from a degree sequence, homogeneous model. Mirrors fit_homogeneous: the ratio L_3/L_2 depends on a alone (the common N factor cancels), a 1-D root find, then N = L_2 / [single-level log E[W^2]](a) from the scale.
test_depth_degrees()
Parametric-bootstrap test of H0: N = N0 (homogeneous a) against a degree sequence D – the factorial-moment analogue of test_depth. fit_homogeneous_network's point estimate has no formal p-value attached; this closes that gap the same way test_depth does for a propensity sequence. A degree sequence whose L3/L2 ratio cannot be matched by any a in the bracket is a genuine model-selection signal (raises, like fit_homogeneous_network), not something papered over.

Maximum entropy

Closing the loop – maximizing S[p] recovers p = B(E)/Z.

target_distribution()
p_i = B(E_i)/Z with Z = sum_i B(E_i). Returns list(p, Z, U) with U = sum_i p_i E_i the mean energy the maximization is constrained to.
maximize()
Maximize S[p] = sum_i Z^{-1} s(Z p_i) under sum_i p_i = 1 and sum_i p_i E_i = U (U taken from target_distribution). Z is held at the partition function of the target, a fixed property of the spectrum, not a variable of the problem. E(B) comes from the tabulated interpolant of make_interpolants (n=800 knots, not the module default of 300: the recovered probabilities inherit the table's accuracy directly, and 300 leaves the power-law class's tail good to only about three digits). SLSQP-equivalent optimization (nloptr's NLOPT_LD_SLSQP) is run twice, the second time warm-started from the first answer: the entropy is very flat near its maximum, so a single pass stops early.
stationarity_residual()
Spread of s'(Z p_i) - beta0*E_i across states: this is the constant alpha at the maximizer, so the spread is zero there. Reported as max - min: a direct, optimizer-free check, and the one that localizes a broken link fastest.
